name: lokalbot-cli
description: Retrieve recorded meetings and separately authorized screen memory on macOS
readme:
# LokalBot **Your personal context engine.** Notes from every call with no bot. One search for everything you saw and heard.
Autocomplete and dictation in any app. Local by default.
Your AI agents can search it too, from Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client. The real app on fictional data. Waits are cut and some typing is sped up. **Free and open source. No account.** [![Download LokalBot for macOS](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E2%80%82Download%20for%20macOS%E2%80%82-Apple%20Silicon-0969da?style=for-the-badge&logo=apple&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest) [![Download LokalBot for Windows (alpha)](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E2%80%82Download%20for%20Windows%E2%80%82-alpha-0969da?style=for-the-badge&logo=data%3Aimage%2Fsvg%2Bxml%3Bbase64%2CPHN2ZyB4bWxucz0naHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmcnIHZpZXdCb3g9JzAgMCAxNiAxNic%2BPHBhdGggZmlsbD0nd2hpdGUnIGQ9J00wIDBoNy41djcuNUgwek04LjUgMEgxNnY3LjVIOC41ek0wIDguNWg3LjVWMTZIMHpNOC41IDguNUgxNlYxNkg4LjV6Jy8%2BPC9zdmc%2B)](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest) [![Download LokalBot for Linux (alpha)](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E2%80%82Download%20for%20Linux%E2%80%82-alpha-0969da?style=for-the-badge&logo=linux&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest) Apple Silicon (M1 or later) with macOS 15+ · Windows 10/11 x64 (alpha) · Linux x86_64 (alpha) · on Mac, also brew install --cask stevyhacker/tap/lokalbot [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/stevyhacker/lokalbot?color=1f6feb&label=release)](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest) [![License: GPLv3](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPLv3-2ea043)](LICENSE) [![MCP: read-only server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-read--only%20server-8250df)](#for-developers--agents) ⭐ If LokalBot is useful to you, star the repo. It's built by one developer, and stars are how other people find it. **English** · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) [Features](#features) · [Agents & CLI](#for-developers--agents) · [Windows & Linux](#windows-and-linux) · [Compare](#how-it-compares) · [Privacy](#privacy) · [Get started](#get-started) · [Models](#local-ai-your-choice) · [Website](https://www.lokalbot.com/)
## Features ### Remember what was agreed Record microphone and meeting-app audio without a bot joining. Get local transcripts, recaps, decisions, and action items, with citations back to the discussion. You can also import audio and video files as meetings.
### Find something you saw One search across your meeting transcripts and, if you turn it on, what you saw on screen. Search by keyword or by meaning, then open the matching passage or screen moment instead of hunting through apps. The same window (**⌃⇧ Space**, or **Ctrl+Shift+Space** on Windows and Linux, once you turn on the shortcut in **Settings → Ask**, or **Settings → General** on Windows and Linux) also runs app commands such as **Record now** or **Start dictation** from whatever app you're in.
### Finish the sentence As you type in other apps, gray text suggests how your sentence ends. Press **Tab** to take the next word, **\`** to take the rest, or keep typing.
Live suggestions in TextEdit, in real time. The ship date and condition come from the meeting with John. Fictional demo meeting.
- **Knows what you're answering.** It reads the message or page above the field, so a reply fits the thread. - **Remembers your meetings, if you let it.** Turn on meeting and work memory, and it can bring in what was decided, like the ship date above. - **Writes in your language.** On Mac, the same small model keeps up in German, French, Italian, Spanish, and more. - **Stays on your computer.** A small model runs inside the app: Gemma 4 E2B on Mac, LFM2.5 1.2B on Windows and Linux. What you type and the context it reads stay on your computer, unless you choose an autocomplete server and approve it. Turn it on in **Settings → Autocomplete**, where you can try it on a sample conversation first and later see how much it wrote for you. ### Pick up where you left off
What do I still need to do?
Today shows the day's summary and every open action, each linked to the meeting it came from. Each morning the overnight review adds a look back at yesterday.		 Where did the day go?
Retrace your day session by session. Tracking starts with app and window activity; screen text and screenshots are opt-in. If you use Claude Code or Codex, it can name the work by project and show related pull requests and commits.
What's open with Maya?
See what's waiting on you and what you decided together. Name a speaker once, and LokalBot recognizes their voice in later meetings.		 Where did I save that?
Search the folders you choose by what's in them: documents, PDF pages, pictures, and moments in recordings and video.
Where does this project stand?
Track a project, and LokalBot gathers the meetings, actions, and decisions that name it. Open it for a short note on where it stands, with links back to the meetings behind it. Not sure what to track? It suggests names that keep coming up in your meetings.
### Ask, then check the source Ask your own work a question. Answers cite their sources, and say so when one can't be verified. Follow a citation back to the transcript or audio. Generated notes are a starting point, not a substitute for the discussion.
### Talk instead of typing Turn on Dictation in **Settings → Dictation**, then hold **⌥ Space** (**Alt+Space** on Windows and Linux, or a shortcut you choose there), speak, and release to insert text at your cursor in any app. Transcription runs on your computer, and your recent dictations are kept so you can copy one again. In Compose mode, say what you need and LokalBot writes it at your cursor, from your meetings if you let it. On Wayland, bind `lokalbot dictate` to a shortcut in your desktop's settings.
### Rewrite what you selected Turn on selection actions in **Settings → Ask** (**Settings → General** on Windows and Linux), select text in any app, and press **⌃⇧ W**. Fix the grammar, make it shorter, translate it, summarize it, or type your own instruction, then replace the selection or copy the result. **Draft a reply with my memory** also searches your meetings, so the reply can use what was actually agreed, and lists the meetings it used. It runs on your Think model, which stays on your computer unless you chose and approved a server. On Windows and Linux the shortcut is **Ctrl+Alt+Space**, because ⌃⇧ W closes tabs and windows there; on Wayland, bind `lokalbot selection-actions` to a shortcut in your desktop's settings. ### It remembers how you work Personal Context is an encrypted list of your facts, preferences, goals, and principles. Tell Ask "Remember I want the agenda the day before," add items in Settings, or let the overnight review pick up facts and preferences from your own words in meetings. Ask uses what it holds, so answers fit your work. - **Only your own words.** It learns from your lines, never other speakers'. The model that reads them stays on your computer unless you approve a server. - **You see where it came from.** Every learned item shows the line behind it. Preferences, and anything from what you typed, wait for you to keep or dismiss them. Facts and goals from meetings are saved directly. - **Yours to turn off.** Learning is on by default, at up to three items a night. One switch in Settings stops it. - **Private from agents.** Agents read only the items you choose to share, under a separate permission. ### Draft the follow-up Prepare local follow-up drafts. Also keep a note for every meeting in your Obsidian or Logseq folder, and get daily briefs and weekly work logs. You review and send them yourself. The clips show the real Mac app on fictional data, with waits cut and some typing sped up. Search, Today, Timeline and People use a seeded library; the notes, Ask answers, dictation, autocomplete and Files results come from the on-device models. How they were made. ### Also on Windows and Linux (alpha) A native Windows and Linux app, written in Rust, has the same pages and reads the same library, so a library moves between computers. Encrypted items, such as Ask history, Personal Context, screenshots, and remembered voices, open only on the computer that saved them. Meetings, transcription, Ask, search, day memory, screen context, dictation, autocomplete, selection actions, spoken summaries, Files, overnight review, Personal Context, calendar, Agent Mode, and the CLI and MCP server all work. It's an alpha: the Windows build isn't code-signed yet, some features depend on your Linux desktop (Wayland support is partial), and Gmail in meeting briefs hasn't been ported. See [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where) and [screenshots](LinuxWindows/docs/screenshots). ## For developers & agents Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client can search your meetings through the bundled **`lokalbot-cli`** or its stdio **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server. Ask what was decided, who owns an action item, or where a topic came up. Agents can read your library but can't change it.
Connect Claude Code with one command, or install the [Claude Code plugin](Distribution/claude-plugin/README.md): ```bash # macOS claude mcp add lokalbot -- /Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli mcp # Windows and Linux, with lokalbot-cli on your PATH claude mcp add lokalbot -- lokalbot-cli mcp ``` Access is off by default. On a Mac, turn on **Allow external agents to read your LokalBot data** in **Settings → External Agents** and tick what agents may read: Meetings, Screen memory, What I shared about myself, or Files. On Windows and Linux, each has its own switch under External agents in **Settings → Privacy & Data**: meeting library, files, screen memory, and What I shared about myself. Then install the CLI from **Settings → External Agents → Agent CLI** on a Mac, or **Settings → Advanced → Agent CLI** on Windows and Linux. **Ready to act on a meeting?** Open any action item in Claude Code or Codex, and the prompt is already typed in with the task and where it came from, for you to review and send. Or use the CLI from any shell or agent: ```bash lokalbot-cli search "database decision" lokalbot-cli get latest --include metadata,summary lokalbot-cli search-files "lease renewal" --kind pdf # with Files access on lokalbot-cli mcp ``` Without a PATH installation, use `/Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli` on Mac. On Windows and Linux, **Settings → Advanced → Agent CLI** installs it too; see [Coding agents](LinuxWindows/README.md#coding-agents) for where it goes and how to add it to your PATH. The commands and MCP tools are the same on every platform. Screen-memory MCP tools require separate permission scoped to today, the last seven days, or all retained history. They return text and metadata, not decrypted screenshots. `search_files` searches the folders you chose under Files by their words and returns file paths, excerpts, and the matched passages; it needs Files access and never changes your files. External clients may send results to their own model providers. The app also has an optional **Agent Mode** for working with reviewed context. File and shell actions follow its approval settings; it is separate from the read-only CLI/MCP interface. [CLI examples](.agents/skills/lokalbot-cli/SKILL.md) · [Claude Code plugin](Distribution/claude-plugin/README.md) · [MCP architecture](DEVELOPMENT.md#agent-cli--mcp) ## How it compares | Coming from… | What's different with LokalBot | | --- | --- | | [Granola](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-granola) | The same bot-free capture, but transcription and summaries run on your computer by default. No account and no subscription. | | [Apple Notes](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-apple-notes) | Notes records your microphone, so with headphones on it misses the other side of a Zoom or Teams call. LokalBot records both sides and keeps every meeting searchable, with notes that cite the discussion. | | [Otter](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-otter) · [Fireflies](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-fireflies) | Nothing joins your call, audio stays on your computer, and there are no minute caps. | | [Hyprnote (anarlog)](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-hyprnote) | Local AI ships built in, with no separate model runner or API keys to set up. Dictation, a day timeline, and autocomplete come in the same app. | | [Meetily](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-meetily) | Both are open source and run locally. Speaker separation, meeting detection, and MCP access are free here rather than Pro features, and dictation, a day timeline, and autocomplete come in the same app. | | [Screenpipe](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-screenpipe) | Starts with app and window activity. Screen text and screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days by default. GPLv3 rather than source-available. | | [Rewind](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-rewind) | Rewind's Mac app is discontinued. LokalBot's timeline is open source and actively developed. | | [MacWhisper](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-macwhisper) · [Superwhisper](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-superwhisper) | Dictation comes alongside meeting notes, recall, and autocomplete, for free. For transcribing files you already have, MacWhisper is the better tool. | | [Wispr Flow](https://www.lokalbot.com/lokalbot-vs-wispr-flow) | Dictation and bot-free meeting notes run on your computer, with no account, word cap, or connection required. Wispr Flow transcribes both in its cloud. | Competitor details were last verified on September 24, 2026, and October 1, 2026 for Apple Notes, Meetily, and Wispr Flow; each link has the full comparison and sources. Trademarks belong to their owners. ## Privacy **Your work is personal. Keeping it local should be the starting point.** Recording and built-in AI processing happen on your computer. LokalBot has no account system, analytics service, or telemetry backend. Your library lives in local files and SQLite under your user account. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph mac [Your computer] direction LR audio["Mic + meeting-app audio"] --> asr["On-device
transcription"] asr --> llm["Local summaries
built-in llama.cpp"] screen["Opt-in screen text"] --> db[("Local library
full-text + vector search")] asr --> db llm --> db db --> use["Search · Ask · Today · Timeline"] db -.->|read-only, off by default| cli["lokalbot-cli · MCP"] end ``` - **You choose what to retain.** Activity-only tracking is the default. Visible screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in. Pause capture or exclude apps and domains at any time. Detection has limits; exclude anything you never want retained. - **You control retention.** Captured screen text and screenshots expire after 14 days by default. Adjust the window or explicitly save a moment to keep it until you unsave or delete it. - **Network access has boundaries.** Models, updates, and optional agent runtimes need downloads. Automatic update checks can be disabled. A remote model server receives context only after you approve its origin; optional Agent Mode and external CLI/MCP clients have separate permissions and data handling. - **Your phone gets a copy only if you pair it.** Settings → Phones & tablets is off by default. When you turn it on, the Mac sends the phones and tablets you pair an end-to-end encrypted copy of the data you choose, over your local network or Tailscale, with no LokalBot server in between. Screenshots, screen text, attendee emails, and voice profiles are never shared. A paired phone can also record a meeting and send it the same way; your Mac processes it, and the phone then deletes its copy. To check the local processing path, download the models, select the built-in backend, disable automatic update checks, and observe network traffic while recording, transcribing, and summarizing. Approved agent commands and external clients are separate paths. [Read the full privacy policy](PRIVACY.md) · [Report a security issue privately](SECURITY.md) ## Get started LokalBot runs on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later. Windows and Linux are in alpha. You'll also need space for your selected models: **Settings → Models** shows download sizes and readiness, and storage and memory needs depend on the models you choose. | | macOS | Windows (alpha) | Linux (alpha) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Runs on | Apple Silicon (M1 or later), macOS 15+ | Windows 10 or 11, x64 | x86_64 with glibc 2.39 or later (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40 or newer), PulseAudio or PipeWire, and a Vulkan or OpenGL driver | | Install | [`LokalBot--macos-arm64.dmg`](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest): drag LokalBot to Applications. Or `brew install --cask stevyhacker/tap/lokalbot`. | [`LokalBot--windows-x86_64-setup.exe`](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest): run it to install LokalBot for your user, with a Start menu shortcut and no administrator rights. It isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen asks first: **More info → Run anyway**. The same release has a portable zip. | [`LokalBot--linux-x86_64.tar.gz`](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest): extract it and run `./install.sh`, which adds LokalBot to your applications menu. Or install the `.deb` (Debian, Ubuntu), `.rpm` (Fedora, openSUSE) or Arch package from the same release. The `.deb`, and the `.rpm` on Fedora, add the LokalBot repository, so `sudo apt upgrade` or `sudo dnf upgrade` brings later versions; with the Arch package, LokalBot tells you about updates instead of installing them. | | Your library | `~/Library/Application Support/me.dotenv.LokalBot` | `%LOCALAPPDATA%\LokalBot` | `~/.local/share/LokalBot` | A library recorded on one platform opens on the others. Not every Mac feature is on Windows and Linux yet; see [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where). 1. **Install the app** for your platform and open it. 2. **Choose what to capture.** Review recording settings: automatic detection, ask-first, or manual recording. Day tracking starts with activity only; saving screen text or screenshots is a separate opt-in. Grant only the permissions for the features you enable. 3. **Let the models download.** Built-in transcription, search, summaries, and writing can then work offline. No model server to set up and no API key to bring. **Try this first:** make a short test recording, let it transcribe, then search for a phrase you said and open the matching passage. Add screen memory or writing tools when you're ready. Let meeting participants know before recording and get their consent. [Release notes](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases) · [Setup help](SUPPORT.md) · [Homebrew options](Distribution/homebrew/README.md) · [Windows and Linux guide](LinuxWindows/README.md) ## FAQ
Does a bot join my meetings? No. LokalBot records your microphone and the meeting app's audio on your computer. On Windows and Linux it records the meeting app alone where it can, and otherwise everything the computer plays. Audio sources are separate from individual speaker identification. When system-audio capture is unavailable, the app warns that recording is microphone-only. Always record with participants' consent.
Does it record everything on my screen? No. New installs use activity-only tracking, which you can turn off. Saving visible text or screenshots requires a separate choice and the relevant macOS permissions (on Linux, your desktop's accessibility and screenshot support). Excluded apps and domains and secure fields are skipped; private browser windows are captured unless you exclude the browser or site. Detected credentials are redacted and associated pixels are dropped, but detection is not perfect. See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md).
Can I take my notes elsewhere? Yes. Turn on **Meeting note export** to keep a Markdown note for every meeting in a folder you choose, such as an Obsidian vault or a Logseq graph: the summary, action items, the people and projects involved, and the transcript. You can also export a single meeting, write a daily memory note, or let local routines save drafts. These are ordinary, unencrypted files; any service you sync them with has its own privacy settings. See [Meeting transcripts in Obsidian](https://www.lokalbot.com/meeting-transcripts-obsidian-markdown).
Does it run on Windows or Linux? Yes, as an alpha. The Windows and Linux app is a native Rust app with the same pages, the same models for summaries and search, and the same library format, so a library moves between computers. Encrypted items, such as Ask history, Personal Context, screenshots, and remembered voices, open only on the computer that saved them. Gmail in meeting briefs is Mac only for now, and on Wayland some features depend on your desktop. See [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where).
## Local AI, your choice Start with the built-in models, then change them in **Settings → Models**. LokalBot supports its bundled llama.cpp runtime, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers, and Apple Intelligence on supported Macs running macOS 26 or later. Think can also run on your own ChatGPT plan (Sign in with ChatGPT) or Claude plan (through your signed-in Claude Code), without an API key, and Agent Mode can run on the ChatGPT plan. Remote servers and plans require approval before receiving context. Different jobs use different models. These are the Mac defaults on a fresh install, about 9.6 GB of model files if you use every role. They are not a RAM requirement: | Role | Default model | Format | Approx. model files | | --- | --- | --- | ---: | | Transcription | Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | MLX 8-bit | 2.47 GB | | Summaries and chat | Qwen3.5 4B | `Q4_K_M` | 2.74 GB | | Autocomplete | Gemma 4 E2B Base | `Q6_K` | 3.85 GB | | Semantic search | EmbeddingGemma 2 | `Q8_0` | 0.31 GB | | Speaker diarization | Nemotron 3 (preview) via FluidAudio | Core ML | ~0.20 GB | The table leaves out helper models, which download when a feature first needs them: with Qwen3-ASR, speaker separation adds a word-timing model of about 1 GB, and turning on Files adds a 555 MB image and audio projector. Qwen3-ASR covers 52 languages and dialects. Transcription alternatives include Parakeet, Granite Speech, Whisper large-v3 turbo, SenseVoice for Chinese, Japanese, and Korean, and GigaAM for Russian; Pyannote Community-1 remains available for diarization. The Lightweight preset swaps in smaller models, including LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct (0.73 GB) for autocomplete. Model choices can vary by release; Settings shows the active selections and available presets. Speed and memory use depend on your computer, model, context length, and other workloads. On Windows and Linux, transcription uses Qwen3-ASR 0.6B through sherpa-onnx (Parakeet v3 and v2, SenseVoice, GigaAM Russian, and Whisper turbo are optional), speakers are separated with pyannote segmentation and TitaNet, and autocomplete uses LFM2.5 1.2B by default. Summaries (Qwen3.5 4B) and search (EmbeddingGemma 2) use the same models as on Mac. The default download is about 4 GB, and llama.cpp runs on a Vulkan GPU or the CPU. [Project benchmarks](Benchmarks/README.md) · [Model catalog](LokalBot/Engines/ModelCatalog.swift) · [Search implementation](LokalBot/Services/EmbeddingIndex.swift) · [Model and runtime details](DEVELOPMENT.md#built-in-llm-runtime--llamacpp--model-catalog) ## Build from source For the Mac app, use an Apple Silicon Mac with full Xcode installed; the [build workflow](.github/workflows/build.yml) pins the CI toolchain. With Homebrew available: ```bash brew install xcodegen cmake # Rust (https://rustup.rs) builds the phone and tablet sync library; the repo # pins the toolchain, which rustup installs on first use. curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain none git clone https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot.git cd lokalbot # XcodeGen needs these paths before the first build fetches the runtimes. mkdir -p Vendor/llama-cpp Vendor/sherpa-onnx # The phone and tablet sync library (Rust), as a local Swift package. Scripts/build-sync-xcframework.sh xcodegen generate open LokalBot.xcodeproj ``` Select **LokalBot Dev**, set your signing team, and run. The Dev app has its own identity, macOS permission grants, library, model storage, and Keychain namespace, so it can live alongside the installed release without applying development retention settings to release data. The first build prepares pinned native runtimes; model downloads happen separately. For the Windows and Linux app, see [Build from source](LinuxWindows/README.md#build-from-source) in its README (Rust). [Build and test commands](DEVELOPMENT.md#build-workflows) · [Testing guide](DEVELOPMENT.md#testing) · [Screenshot guide](Docs/screenshot-kit.md)
Find your way around the code ```text LokalBot/ ├── Views/ # Native SwiftUI screens, settings, and onboarding ├── Services/ # Recording, search, storage, and workday memory ├── Engines/ # Transcription, model catalog, and local inference ├── Cotyping/ # System-wide autocomplete ├── Dictation/ # Voice typing └── Agent/ # Optional Agent Mode and approval flow CLI/ # Command-line interface and MCP entry points LinuxWindows/ # Windows and Linux app (Rust + GPUI) LokalBotTests/ # Unit tests Scripts/ # Build, verification, capture, and release tooling project.yml # XcodeGen source of truth ```
## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, and code contributions are welcome. [Report an issue](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/issues/new/choose) with steps to reproduce, expected and actual behavior, the app version, your OS and its version (on Linux, also the distribution, desktop, and X11 or Wayland), your chip or CPU and GPU, RAM, and selected models. Keep private recordings and transcripts out of reports. For larger changes, [open an issue](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/issues) to discuss the approach first. Follow the [working agreements](AGENTS.md) and [development guide](DEVELOPMENT.md), keep pull requests focused, and record your checks in the [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Include screenshots for UI changes; run UI tests on hosted CI or a remote runner. ## License & acknowledgements LokalBot is free software under [GPLv3](LICENSE). Code in the Autocomplete engine that was ported from [Cotabby](https://github.com/FuJacob/cotabby) stays under [AGPLv3](LICENSES/AGPL-3.0.txt). Other third-party components and models retain their own licenses; see [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Built with [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp), [MLX Swift](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-swift), [speech-swift](https://github.com/soniqo/speech-swift), [sherpa-onnx](https://github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx), [WhisperKit](https://github.com/argmaxinc/WhisperKit), [FluidAudio](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio), [Sparkle](https://github.com/sparkle-project/Sparkle), [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen), [GPUI](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/tree/main/crates/gpui), [GPUI Kit](https://github.com/longbridge/gpui-kit), and [ONNX Runtime](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime), with models including [Qwen3-ASR](https://huggingface.co/Qwen), [IBM Granite Speech](https://huggingface.co/ibm-granite), [Parakeet](https://huggingface.co/nvidia), and [LFM2.5](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI). The Autocomplete engine started from [Cotabby](https://cotabby.app)'s open-source code.

LokalBot

Your personal context engine.

Notes from every call with no bot. One search for everything you saw and heard.<br />

Autocomplete and dictation in any app. Local by default.<br />

Your AI agents can search it too, from Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client.

<picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="Assets/hero/lokalbot-demo-dark.gif" /><img src="Assets/hero/lokalbot-demo-light.gif" width="920" alt="LokalBot in use, in six looping scenes with fictional demo data, each under a caption. Notes from every call, with no bot: a Google Chrome call is recorded, its live transcript fills in, the notes appear, and clicking an action item's citation opens the transcript at that line. One search for everything you saw and heard: typing "demo pres" finds a Keynote deck and a Mail reply seen on screen, and two meetings. Autocomplete that knows what your meetings decided: in TextEdit, it finishes "the Team plan will be $15" with "per seat, billed annually." and Tab accepts it. Say what you need, and it writes at your cursor: holding Option-Space writes a short team update into an empty document. Ask your own work, then check the source: an answer about a holiday shoot cites a meeting, and clicking the citation opens it. Your AI agents can search it too: in a terminal, Claude Code calls LokalBot and lists what a design review decided and what is still owed." /></picture>

Features

Remember what was agreed

Record microphone and meeting-app audio without a bot joining. Get local transcripts, recaps, decisions, and action items, with citations back to the discussion. You can also import audio and video files as meetings.

<div align="center"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="Assets/readme/meetings-dark.png" /><img src="Assets/readme/meetings-light.png" width="800" alt="A recorded call's notes: audio playback, a recap of what was decided, and action items, each with the time it was said" /></picture></div>

Find something you saw

One search across your meeting transcripts and, if you turn it on, what you saw on screen. Search by keyword or by meaning, then open the matching passage or screen moment instead of hunting through apps. The same window (⌃⇧ Space, or Ctrl+Shift+Space on Windows and Linux, once you turn on the shortcut in Settings → Ask, or Settings → General on Windows and Linux) also runs app commands such as Record now or Start dictation from whatever app you're in.

<div align="center"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="Assets/readme/search-dark.png" /><img src="Assets/readme/search-light.png" width="640" alt="Quick Recall finding a Keynote deck and a Mail reply seen on screen, and two meetings that mention the demo presentation" /></picture></div>

Finish the sentence

As you type in other apps, gray text suggests how your sentence ends. Press Tab to take the next word, \` to take the rest, or keep typing.

<div align="center"><img src="Assets/screenshots/autocomplete-memory.gif" alt="Typing an update in TextEdit after a call with John: after "the Harbor beta ships", autocomplete suggests "Thursday morning, after the accessibility review." and Tab accepts it word by word" width="920" /></div>

<div align="center"><sub>Live suggestions in TextEdit, in real time. The ship date and condition come from the meeting with John. Fictional demo meeting.</sub></div>

  • Knows what you're answering. It reads the message or page above the field, so a reply fits the thread.
  • Remembers your meetings, if you let it. Turn on meeting and work memory, and it can bring in what was decided, like the ship date above.
  • Writes in your language. On Mac, the same small model keeps up in German, French, Italian, Spanish, and more.
  • Stays on your computer. A small model runs inside the app: Gemma 4 E2B on Mac, LFM2.5 1.2B on Windows and Linux. What you type and the context it reads stay on your computer, unless you choose an autocomplete server and approve it.

Turn it on in Settings → Autocomplete, where you can try it on a sample conversation first and later see how much it wrote for you.

Ask, then check the source

Ask your own work a question. Answers cite their sources, and say so when one can't be verified. Follow a citation back to the transcript or audio. Generated notes are a starting point, not a substitute for the discussion.

<div align="center"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="Assets/readme/ask-dark.gif" /><img src="Assets/readme/ask-light.gif" width="720" alt="Asking what was decided about the shoot: the answer streams in with numbered citations and an evidence list, and clicking the source opens the Holiday shoot planning meeting" /></picture></div>

Talk instead of typing

Turn on Dictation in Settings → Dictation, then hold ⌥ Space (Alt+Space on Windows and Linux, or a shortcut you choose there), speak, and release to insert text at your cursor in any app. Transcription runs on your computer, and your recent dictations are kept so you can copy one again. In Compose mode, say what you need and LokalBot writes it at your cursor, from your meetings if you let it. On Wayland, bind lokalbot dictate to a shortcut in your desktop's settings.

<div align="center"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="Assets/readme/dictation-dark.gif" /><img src="Assets/readme/dictation-light.gif" width="720" alt="Holding Option-Space to dictate into an empty document: a small panel listens, then a short team update with the launch pricing appears at the cursor" /></picture></div>

Rewrite what you selected

Turn on selection actions in Settings → Ask (Settings → General on Windows and Linux), select text in any app, and press ⌃⇧ W. Fix the grammar, make it shorter, translate it, summarize it, or type your own instruction, then replace the selection or copy the result. Draft a reply with my memory also searches your meetings, so the reply can use what was actually agreed, and lists the meetings it used. It runs on your Think model, which stays on your computer unless you chose and approved a server. On Windows and Linux the shortcut is Ctrl+Alt+Space, because ⌃⇧ W closes tabs and windows there; on Wayland, bind lokalbot selection-actions to a shortcut in your desktop's settings.

It remembers how you work

Personal Context is an encrypted list of your facts, preferences, goals, and principles. Tell Ask "Remember I want the agenda the day before," add items in Settings, or let the overnight review pick up facts and preferences from your own words in meetings. Ask uses what it holds, so answers fit your work.

  • Only your own words. It learns from your lines, never other speakers'. The model that reads them stays on your computer unless you approve a server.
  • You see where it came from. Every learned item shows the line behind it. Preferences, and anything from what you typed, wait for you to keep or dismiss them. Facts and goals from meetings are saved directly.
  • Yours to turn off. Learning is on by default, at up to three items a night. One switch in Settings stops it.
  • Private from agents. Agents read only the items you choose to share, under a separate permission.

Draft the follow-up

Prepare local follow-up drafts. Also keep a note for every meeting in your Obsidian or Logseq folder, and get daily briefs and weekly work logs. You review and send them yourself.

<sub>The clips show the real Mac app on fictional data, with waits cut and some typing sped up. Search, Today, Timeline and People use a seeded library; the notes, Ask answers, dictation, autocomplete and Files results come from the on-device models. <a href="Video/lokalbot-landing-demos/README.md">How they were made</a>.</sub>

<a id="windows-and-linux"></a>

Also on Windows and Linux (alpha)

A native Windows and Linux app, written in Rust, has the same pages and reads the same library, so a library moves between computers. Encrypted items, such as Ask history, Personal Context, screenshots, and remembered voices, open only on the computer that saved them. Meetings, transcription, Ask, search, day memory, screen context, dictation, autocomplete, selection actions, spoken summaries, Files, overnight review, Personal Context, calendar, Agent Mode, and the CLI and MCP server all work. It's an alpha: the Windows build isn't code-signed yet, some features depend on your Linux desktop (Wayland support is partial), and Gmail in meeting briefs hasn't been ported. See [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where) and [screenshots](LinuxWindows/docs/screenshots).

For developers & agents

Claude Code, Codex, or any MCP client can search your meetings through the bundled lokalbot-cli or its stdio Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Ask what was decided, who owns an action item, or where a topic came up. Agents can read your library but can't change it.

<div align="center"><picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="Assets/readme/agents-dark.gif" /><img src="Assets/readme/agents-light.gif" width="720" alt="In a terminal, Claude Code is asked what today's design review decided about caching and what is still owed; it calls LokalBot twice and lists the decisions and the open actions" /></picture></div>

Connect Claude Code with one command, or install the [Claude Code plugin](Distribution/claude-plugin/README.md):


# macOS

claude mcp add lokalbot -- /Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli mcp

# Windows and Linux, with lokalbot-cli on your PATH

claude mcp add lokalbot -- lokalbot-cli mcp

Access is off by default. On a Mac, turn on Allow external agents to read your LokalBot data in Settings → External Agents and tick what agents may read: Meetings, Screen memory, What I shared about myself, or Files. On Windows and Linux, each has its own switch under External agents in Settings → Privacy & Data: meeting library, files, screen memory, and What I shared about myself. Then install the CLI from Settings → External Agents → Agent CLI on a Mac, or Settings → Advanced → Agent CLI on Windows and Linux.

Ready to act on a meeting? Open any action item in Claude Code or Codex, and the prompt is already typed in with the task and where it came from, for you to review and send.

Or use the CLI from any shell or agent:


lokalbot-cli search "database decision"

lokalbot-cli get latest --include metadata,summary

lokalbot-cli search-files "lease renewal" --kind pdf   # with Files access on

lokalbot-cli mcp

Without a PATH installation, use /Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli on Mac. On Windows and Linux, Settings → Advanced → Agent CLI installs it too; see [Coding agents](LinuxWindows/README.md#coding-agents) for where it goes and how to add it to your PATH. The commands and MCP tools are the same on every platform.

Screen-memory MCP tools require separate permission scoped to today, the last seven days, or all retained history. They return text and metadata, not decrypted screenshots. search_files searches the folders you chose under Files by their words and returns file paths, excerpts, and the matched passages; it needs Files access and never changes your files. External clients may send results to their own model providers.

The app also has an optional Agent Mode for working with reviewed context. File and shell actions follow its approval settings; it is separate from the read-only CLI/MCP interface.

[CLI examples](.agents/skills/lokalbot-cli/SKILL.md) · [Claude Code plugin](Distribution/claude-plugin/README.md) · [MCP architecture](DEVELOPMENT.md#agent-cli--mcp)

How it compares

| Coming from… | What's different with LokalBot |

| --- | --- |

| Granola | The same bot-free capture, but transcription and summaries run on your computer by default. No account and no subscription. |

| Apple Notes | Notes records your microphone, so with headphones on it misses the other side of a Zoom or Teams call. LokalBot records both sides and keeps every meeting searchable, with notes that cite the discussion. |

| Otter · Fireflies | Nothing joins your call, audio stays on your computer, and there are no minute caps. |

| Hyprnote (anarlog) | Local AI ships built in, with no separate model runner or API keys to set up. Dictation, a day timeline, and autocomplete come in the same app. |

| Meetily | Both are open source and run locally. Speaker separation, meeting detection, and MCP access are free here rather than Pro features, and dictation, a day timeline, and autocomplete come in the same app. |

| Screenpipe | Starts with app and window activity. Screen text and screenshots are opt-in and deleted after 14 days by default. GPLv3 rather than source-available. |

| Rewind | Rewind's Mac app is discontinued. LokalBot's timeline is open source and actively developed. |

| MacWhisper · Superwhisper | Dictation comes alongside meeting notes, recall, and autocomplete, for free. For transcribing files you already have, MacWhisper is the better tool. |

| Wispr Flow | Dictation and bot-free meeting notes run on your computer, with no account, word cap, or connection required. Wispr Flow transcribes both in its cloud. |

<sub>Competitor details were last verified on September 24, 2026, and October 1, 2026 for Apple Notes, Meetily, and Wispr Flow; each link has the full comparison and sources. Trademarks belong to their owners.</sub>

<a id="privacy--verify-it"></a>

Privacy

Your work is personal. Keeping it local should be the starting point.

Recording and built-in AI processing happen on your computer. LokalBot has no account system, analytics service, or telemetry backend. Your library lives in local files and SQLite under your user account.


flowchart LR

  subgraph mac [Your computer]

    direction LR

    audio["Mic + meeting-app audio"] --> asr["On-device<br/>transcription"]

    asr --> llm["Local summaries<br/>built-in llama.cpp"]

    screen["Opt-in screen text"] --> db[("Local library<br/>full-text + vector search")]

    asr --> db

    llm --> db

    db --> use["Search · Ask · Today · Timeline"]

    db -.->|read-only, off by default| cli["lokalbot-cli · MCP"]

  end
  • You choose what to retain. Activity-only tracking is the default. Visible screen text and encrypted screenshots are opt-in. Pause capture or exclude apps and domains at any time. Detection has limits; exclude anything you never want retained.
  • You control retention. Captured screen text and screenshots expire after 14 days by default. Adjust the window or explicitly save a moment to keep it until you unsave or delete it.
  • Network access has boundaries. Models, updates, and optional agent runtimes need downloads. Automatic update checks can be disabled. A remote model server receives context only after you approve its origin; optional Agent Mode and external CLI/MCP clients have separate permissions and data handling.
  • Your phone gets a copy only if you pair it. Settings → Phones & tablets is off by default. When you turn it on, the Mac sends the phones and tablets you pair an end-to-end encrypted copy of the data you choose, over your local network or Tailscale, with no LokalBot server in between. Screenshots, screen text, attendee emails, and voice profiles are never shared. A paired phone can also record a meeting and send it the same way; your Mac processes it, and the phone then deletes its copy.

To check the local processing path, download the models, select the built-in backend, disable automatic update checks, and observe network traffic while recording, transcribing, and summarizing. Approved agent commands and external clients are separate paths.

[Read the full privacy policy](PRIVACY.md) · [Report a security issue privately](SECURITY.md)

<a id="download"></a>

Get started

LokalBot runs on Apple Silicon Macs with macOS 15 or later. Windows and Linux are in alpha. You'll also need space for your selected models: Settings → Models shows download sizes and readiness, and storage and memory needs depend on the models you choose.

| | macOS | Windows (alpha) | Linux (alpha) |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Runs on | Apple Silicon (M1 or later), macOS 15+ | Windows 10 or 11, x64 | x86_64 with glibc 2.39 or later (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 40 or newer), PulseAudio or PipeWire, and a Vulkan or OpenGL driver |

| Install | LokalBot-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg: drag LokalBot to Applications. Or brew install --cask stevyhacker/tap/lokalbot. | LokalBot-<version>-windows-x86_64-setup.exe: run it to install LokalBot for your user, with a Start menu shortcut and no administrator rights. It isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen asks first: More info → Run anyway. The same release has a portable zip. | LokalBot-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz: extract it and run ./install.sh, which adds LokalBot to your applications menu. Or install the .deb (Debian, Ubuntu), .rpm (Fedora, openSUSE) or Arch package from the same release. The .deb, and the .rpm on Fedora, add the LokalBot repository, so sudo apt upgrade or sudo dnf upgrade brings later versions; with the Arch package, LokalBot tells you about updates instead of installing them. |

| Your library | ~/Library/Application Support/me.dotenv.LokalBot | %LOCALAPPDATA%\LokalBot | ~/.local/share/LokalBot |

A library recorded on one platform opens on the others. Not every Mac feature is on Windows and Linux yet; see [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where).

1. Install the app for your platform and open it.

2. Choose what to capture. Review recording settings: automatic detection, ask-first, or manual recording. Day tracking starts with activity only; saving screen text or screenshots is a separate opt-in. Grant only the permissions for the features you enable.

3. Let the models download. Built-in transcription, search, summaries, and writing can then work offline. No model server to set up and no API key to bring.

Try this first: make a short test recording, let it transcribe, then search for a phrase you said and open the matching passage. Add screen memory or writing tools when you're ready.

Let meeting participants know before recording and get their consent.

FAQ

<details>

<summary><strong>Does a bot join my meetings?</strong></summary>

No. LokalBot records your microphone and the meeting app's audio on your computer. On Windows and Linux it records the meeting app alone where it can, and otherwise everything the computer plays. Audio sources are separate from individual speaker identification. When system-audio capture is unavailable, the app warns that recording is microphone-only. Always record with participants' consent.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>Does it record everything on my screen?</strong></summary>

No. New installs use activity-only tracking, which you can turn off. Saving visible text or screenshots requires a separate choice and the relevant macOS permissions (on Linux, your desktop's accessibility and screenshot support). Excluded apps and domains and secure fields are skipped; private browser windows are captured unless you exclude the browser or site. Detected credentials are redacted and associated pixels are dropped, but detection is not perfect. See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md).

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>Can I take my notes elsewhere?</strong></summary>

Yes. Turn on Meeting note export to keep a Markdown note for every meeting in a folder you choose, such as an Obsidian vault or a Logseq graph: the summary, action items, the people and projects involved, and the transcript. You can also export a single meeting, write a daily memory note, or let local routines save drafts. These are ordinary, unencrypted files; any service you sync them with has its own privacy settings. See Meeting transcripts in Obsidian.

</details>

<details>

<summary><strong>Does it run on Windows or Linux?</strong></summary>

Yes, as an alpha. The Windows and Linux app is a native Rust app with the same pages, the same models for summaries and search, and the same library format, so a library moves between computers. Encrypted items, such as Ask history, Personal Context, screenshots, and remembered voices, open only on the computer that saved them. Gmail in meeting briefs is Mac only for now, and on Wayland some features depend on your desktop. See [what works where](LinuxWindows/README.md#what-works-where).

</details>

Local AI, your choice

Start with the built-in models, then change them in Settings → Models. LokalBot supports its bundled llama.cpp runtime, Ollama, OpenAI-compatible servers, and Apple Intelligence on supported Macs running macOS 26 or later. Think can also run on your own ChatGPT plan (Sign in with ChatGPT) or Claude plan (through your signed-in Claude Code), without an API key, and Agent Mode can run on the ChatGPT plan. Remote servers and plans require approval before receiving context.

Different jobs use different models. These are the Mac defaults on a fresh install, about 9.6 GB of model files if you use every role. They are not a RAM requirement:

| Role | Default model | Format | Approx. model files |

| --- | --- | --- | ---: |

| Transcription | Qwen3-ASR 1.7B | MLX 8-bit | 2.47 GB |

| Summaries and chat | Qwen3.5 4B | Q4_K_M | 2.74 GB |

| Autocomplete | Gemma 4 E2B Base | Q6_K | 3.85 GB |

| Semantic search | EmbeddingGemma 2 | Q8_0 | 0.31 GB |

| Speaker diarization | Nemotron 3 (preview) via FluidAudio | Core ML | ~0.20 GB |

The table leaves out helper models, which download when a feature first needs them: with Qwen3-ASR, speaker separation adds a word-timing model of about 1 GB, and turning on Files adds a 555 MB image and audio projector.

Qwen3-ASR covers 52 languages and dialects. Transcription alternatives include Parakeet, Granite Speech, Whisper large-v3 turbo, SenseVoice for Chinese, Japanese, and Korean, and GigaAM for Russian; Pyannote Community-1 remains available for diarization. The Lightweight preset swaps in smaller models, including LFM2.5 1.2B Instruct (0.73 GB) for autocomplete. Model choices can vary by release; Settings shows the active selections and available presets. Speed and memory use depend on your computer, model, context length, and other workloads.

On Windows and Linux, transcription uses Qwen3-ASR 0.6B through sherpa-onnx (Parakeet v3 and v2, SenseVoice, GigaAM Russian, and Whisper turbo are optional), speakers are separated with pyannote segmentation and TitaNet, and autocomplete uses LFM2.5 1.2B by default. Summaries (Qwen3.5 4B) and search (EmbeddingGemma 2) use the same models as on Mac. The default download is about 4 GB, and llama.cpp runs on a Vulkan GPU or the CPU.

[Project benchmarks](Benchmarks/README.md) · [Model catalog](LokalBot/Engines/ModelCatalog.swift) · [Search implementation](LokalBot/Services/EmbeddingIndex.swift) · [Model and runtime details](DEVELOPMENT.md#built-in-llm-runtime--llamacpp--model-catalog)

Build from source

For the Mac app, use an Apple Silicon Mac with full Xcode installed; the [build workflow](.github/workflows/build.yml) pins the CI toolchain. With Homebrew available:


brew install xcodegen cmake

# Rust (https://rustup.rs) builds the phone and tablet sync library; the repo

# pins the toolchain, which rustup installs on first use.

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain none



git clone https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot.git

cd lokalbot



# XcodeGen needs these paths before the first build fetches the runtimes.

mkdir -p Vendor/llama-cpp Vendor/sherpa-onnx

# The phone and tablet sync library (Rust), as a local Swift package.

Scripts/build-sync-xcframework.sh

xcodegen generate

open LokalBot.xcodeproj

Select LokalBot Dev, set your signing team, and run. The Dev app has its own identity, macOS permission grants, library, model storage, and Keychain namespace, so it can live alongside the installed release without applying development retention settings to release data. The first build prepares pinned native runtimes; model downloads happen separately.

For the Windows and Linux app, see [Build from source](LinuxWindows/README.md#build-from-source) in its README (Rust).

<a id="contributing--security"></a>

Contributing

Bug reports, documentation improvements, and code contributions are welcome. Report an issue with steps to reproduce, expected and actual behavior, the app version, your OS and its version (on Linux, also the distribution, desktop, and X11 or Wayland), your chip or CPU and GPU, RAM, and selected models. Keep private recordings and transcripts out of reports.

For larger changes, open an issue to discuss the approach first. Follow the [working agreements](AGENTS.md) and [development guide](DEVELOPMENT.md), keep pull requests focused, and record your checks in the [PR template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Include screenshots for UI changes; run UI tests on hosted CI or a remote runner.

License & acknowledgements

LokalBot is free software under [GPLv3](LICENSE). Code in the Autocomplete engine that was ported from Cotabby stays under [AGPLv3](LICENSES/AGPL-3.0.txt). Other third-party components and models retain their own licenses; see [third-party notices](THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

# LokalBot CLI Skill

LokalBot is a private work-memory app for macOS, Linux and Windows. Its read-only CLI retrieves recorded meetings and searches the folders the user chose under Files; separately authorized MCP tools retrieve screen-memory text and metadata. Use this skill for evidence from the user's recorded work, not for scheduling meetings or answering general questions about a topic.

If `lokalbot-cli` isn't on PATH, use the embedded copy directly:
`/Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli`.
Windows and Linux installs put it at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\LokalBot\bin\lokalbot-cli.exe` (Windows) or `~/.local/bin/lokalbot-cli` (Linux).

## Start here

```bash
lokalbot-cli brief
```

Run this once at the start of a session (MCP: `get_briefing`). It says which LokalBot sources are on and how the user would turn on the others, then gives what each permission covers: what the user shared about themselves, their open action items, current projects and goals, recent Claude Code and Codex work by project, and a timeline with recent days in detail and older weeks and months in a line each. It is short on purpose. Use it to orient, then search for detail. `brief` points to `lokalbot-cli` commands; `get_briefing` gives the same text but names MCP tools instead.

Before asking the user about past work, a decision, a commitment, or where something stands, search LokalBot first. Ask only when LokalBot has nothing, and say what you checked. Items the briefing doesn't list are unknown, not false. Cite meetings from `get`, `search`, or `actions` results, not from the briefing's summary lines.

## Choose the source

- Use `list` when you need candidate meeting ids, titles, and dates.
- Use `list --include summary` for what several meetings covered, such as the topics of the last ten meetings or one week's themes. One call returns every summary, shortened to fit. Don't fetch transcripts meeting by meeting for that: they are long, and ten of them can fill your context.
- Use `get` when the meeting is known; `latest` works without listing first. Request `metadata,summary` for a cited summary; include `transcript` when the question needs exact wording.
- Use `search` directly when the user remembers a phrase or wants cross-meeting mentions.
- Use `actions` for commitments: what the user owes, overdue work, or one meeting's next steps.
- Use `people` for everything about one person: what the user owes them, what they owe the user, decisions made together, and shared meetings.
- Use `path` only when the task needs an on-disk folder or audio file.
- For viewed screen text or app activity, use the screen-memory MCP tools within the user's separate permission and history scope.
- Use `search-files` (MCP: `search_files`) for something in the user's own documents, PDFs, screenshots, or pictures, such as a contract clause, a receipt, or an error they took a screenshot of.
- Use `personal-context` (MCP: `get_personal_context`) before advising on a personal decision or tailoring work to the user: it returns the facts, preferences, goals, and principles the user chose to share, most relevant to your task first.

## Discovery

```bash
lokalbot-cli list --limit 10
lokalbot-cli list --limit 10 --table
lokalbot-cli list --since 2026-06-01 --query "design"
lokalbot-cli list --limit 10 --include summary
lokalbot-cli list --since 2026-10-13 --until 2026-10-17 --include summary --table
```

The `id` field in each list entry is an 8-character prefix that the other commands accept.

`--include summary` adds each meeting's `summary` (Markdown). The listed summaries share 20,000 characters: short ones come whole, and a long one is cut, ending in `…`, with `"summary_truncated": true`. `get <id> --include summary` reads it whole. With `--include summary`, `--limit` defaults to 10 and goes up to 50. `transcript` isn't accepted there; read transcripts one meeting at a time with `get`.

## Reading a single meeting

```bash
lokalbot-cli get latest --include metadata,summary
lokalbot-cli get 4f7c2a91 --include metadata,summary --format json
lokalbot-cli get 4f7c2a91 --include metadata,transcript
```

`--include` accepts a comma-separated list of `metadata`, `summary`, `transcript`. Default is all three.

## Cross-meeting search

```bash
lokalbot-cli search "auth refactor"
lokalbot-cli search "auth refactor" --table --limit 20
```

A meeting matches when it contains every word, in any order, ignoring case and accents; when none does, the closest partial matches follow. Words of up to three letters or digits (`API`, `Q3`) match only whole words. Quote an exact phrase inside the query (`'"auth refactor"'`) to match only that phrase. Transcript hits include a `timestamp` (HH:MM:SS) so the user can jump to that moment in the in-app player.

## Answers and reply drafts

```bash
lokalbot-cli ask "What did we decide about the caching layer?"
lokalbot-cli reply "Did you pick a caching layer yet?" --instruction "keep it short"
pbpaste | lokalbot-cli reply
```

`ask` is the command-line form of `ask_library` (below): LokalBot's local model answers from the matching meetings. `reply` drafts the user's reply to a message they received from what the matching meetings say, without inventing facts; a message no meeting matches gets no draft. Both need the LokalBot app running, and the first call after a cold start can take up to a minute. JSON by default: `{"status", "text", "sources"}`, where `status` is `answered`, `not_found`, or `error` (with a `code` such as `access_disabled`); errors also exit with status 1. Show a draft to the user before sending it anywhere.

## Action items

```bash
lokalbot-cli actions
lokalbot-cli actions --owner me --table
lokalbot-cli actions --owner ana --status all --days 90
lokalbot-cli actions --meeting 4f7c2a91
```

Actions use the user's saved corrections and status. `due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) appears only when the spoken due phrase resolves unambiguously; otherwise use `due` as said. Overdue and soon-due work comes first.

## People

```bash
lokalbot-cli people --table
lokalbot-cli people --query ana
lokalbot-cli people "Ana Petrović"
```

People are joined from calendar attendee names, speaker names applied in LokalBot, and action owners. Names chosen, people merged, and entries hidden on the app's People page apply here too, and `meeting_count` counts a call recorded in several parts once. Only names are returned; never ask for or infer email addresses.

## Personal context

```bash
lokalbot-cli personal-context --task "Evaluate a job offer in Berlin"
lokalbot-cli personal-context --task "Plan next quarter" --kind goal --kind principle --limit 5
```

Items are what the user chose to share with agents. Each has an `authority`: `"stated"` items are the user's own words; `"learned"` items were picked up by LokalBot from what the user said in meetings, typed or dictated, or from their work, and may be out of date, so don't present one as something the user told you. Each item's `source` says where it came from. Use them only when they bear on the task, and say which ones shaped your answer. Items not returned are unknown, not false, so don't infer the user's values from their absence. They are not evidence about meetings or other people. A `[personal_context_disabled]` error means the user hasn't ticked What I shared about myself (see [When access is off](#when-access-is-off)). Explain that, and don't work around it. The user marks the items agents may read with **Share with Agents** in Settings → Personal Context.

## Files

```bash
lokalbot-cli search-files "lease renewal"
lokalbot-cli search-files "payment declined" --kind screenshot --after 2026-10-01 --table
lokalbot-cli search-files "quarterly report" --kind pdf --kind doc --limit 5
```

Searches only the folders the user chose under Files in LokalBot: the text LokalBot read from documents, PDF pages, screenshots, and pictures, plus file names, best match first. It matches words, not meaning, so use words the file would contain and rephrase when nothing comes back; search by meaning is in LokalBot's Ask. Recordings and video match only by name. Each result has `path`, `kind`, `page` (PDFs) or `seconds`, `modified`, `taken` (photos), `size`, `excerpt`, and `passage`, the matched text up to 1,500 characters. `--kind` takes `screenshot`, `image`, `pdf`, `doc`, `audio`, or `video` and repeats; `--after` and `--before` take YYYY-MM-DD; `--limit` goes up to 50 (default 10). It works with the app closed.

Cite files by path. Open one yourself only when the passage isn't enough, and never change, move, or delete it. `[files_unavailable]` means Files is off in LokalBot, has no folder, or hasn't read its folders yet; the user chooses folders in Settings → Files.

## Path lookup

```bash
lokalbot-cli path
lokalbot-cli path latest                         # the newest meeting's folder
```

## Settings and status

Use these when the user asks how LokalBot is set up, why something is or isn't happening (recording, capture, models), or wants a setting changed.

```bash
lokalbot-cli config search "dark mode"           # find a setting's key by plain words
lokalbot-cli config describe autoRecordMode      # type, allowed values, tier
lokalbot-cli config get autoRecordMode
lokalbot-cli config list --changed --table
lokalbot-cli config set noteTemplate=lecture summaryLanguage=en
lokalbot-cli config set trackingEnabled=false --dry-run
lokalbot-cli config reset dayDigestHour
lokalbot-cli config export --changed > settings.json
lokalbot-cli config import settings.json --dry-run
lokalbot-cli config set calendarDetectionEnabled=true --wait 120   # waits for the user's approval
lokalbot-cli config request <id> --wait 120      # answer to an earlier needs_approval
lokalbot-cli secret list                         # which API keys are saved (never their values)
lokalbot-cli secret set openai-compatible --wait 120   # the key goes in on standard input
lokalbot-cli status                              # version, recording, models, permissions, agent access
lokalbot-cli open settings dictationShortcut     # show the user a setting in LokalBot
lokalbot-cli open settings permissions           # or a section
lokalbot-cli open settings filesAccess           # the Files box; also agentAccess, screenMemoryAccess, personalContextAccess
```

`search`, `describe`, and `config schema` work any time. Everything else needs the separate "Allow external agents to change LokalBot settings" toggle in LokalBot → Settings → External Agents (Settings → Privacy & Data on Windows and Linux). If a command returns `[settings_access_disabled]`, explain that setting and let the user choose. These commands start LokalBot in the background when it isn't running; pass `--no-launch` when the user doesn't want it started.

Changing settings:

- Change only what the user asked for. Run `describe` first so you use the right tokens, and `--dry-run` when you are unsure. A `set` applies all of its pairs or none of them.
- Preferences (tier `preference`), and changes that narrow what LokalBot captures or sends (turning capture off, adding an exclusion), apply right away. The user can undo them under the toggle.
- Turning on capture, a data source, autocomplete or dictation, approving a server, removing an exclusion, or changing retention (tier `consent`) sends the whole request to the user in LokalBot and returns `[needs_approval]` (exit 3) with the request in `details`: its `id`, every change, and, for a shorter retention policy, what the cleanup deletes. Nothing is applied yet. Ask the user before making such a request, tell them a card is waiting in LokalBot, and pass `--wait <seconds>` (up to 300) or run `config request <id> --wait <seconds>` for the answer: exit 0 approved, 4 declined, 5 expired. Don't resend a declined request unless the user asks; an identical request still waiting is reused rather than asked twice.
- API keys: `secret set <name>` reads the key from standard input and always waits for approval the same way. Never put a key on the command line, never echo it back, and never ask to read one; `secret list` only says whether each is saved. `secret clear <name>` removes one right away.
- `[read_only]` settings can't be changed from the terminal.
- Never write LokalBot's preferences with `defaults write`, and never create or edit files in its `control/` folder: a partial preferences write silently resets other settings (it can turn automatic recording on), and the running app overwrites it anyway.

## Setting up LokalBot

When the user wants LokalBot set up, run these steps in order; `lokalbot-cli <command> --help` describes each command. If LokalBot isn't installed yet, install it first: on a Mac with `brew install --cask stevyhacker/tap/lokalbot`, and on Windows and Linux from the [latest release](https://github.com/stevyhacker/lokalbot/releases/latest), after which the user picks what LokalBot remembers in the app. On Windows and Linux the same commands work once the app is running; those systems have no permission prompts, so `permissions` says what the desktop allows.

```bash
lokalbot-cli setup start --wait 300        # the user clicks Allow in LokalBot; the only way to get access
lokalbot-cli setup plan > plan.json        # talk it through, then edit to the user's answers
lokalbot-cli setup apply plan.json --wait 300
lokalbot-cli models status                 # poll until meetingReady
lokalbot-cli permissions                   # then: permissions request <name>, restart if macOS asks
lokalbot-cli setup finish
lokalbot-cli doctor                        # exit 0 when ready; nextSteps otherwise
```

- Ask before adding `--meeting-library`, `--screen-memory`, or `--files` to `setup start`, and before requesting any setting in the plan's `notes.needsApproval`.
- Exit 3 means the user hasn't answered yet, 4 means they declined (don't ask again unless they say so), and 5 means the request expired. `[settings_access_disabled]` means the user hasn't allowed access yet: run `setup start`.
- For permissions, tell the user exactly what to click, then poll `permissions` until it shows the grant.
- Never install by removing the quarantine attribute, and never write LokalBot's preferences or files in `control/` yourself.

## MCP alternative (and ask_library)

The same library is available over MCP for GUI clients and anything else that speaks it: `lokalbot-cli mcp` serves `get_briefing` (call it first; same text as `brief`), `list_meetings` (`include: "summary"` works as in `list --include summary`), `get_meeting`, `search_meetings`, `ask_library`, `get_action_items`, `list_people`, and `get_person` on stdio. It also advertises `search_screen`, `get_timeline`, `get_recent_activity`, `get_app_usage`, and `get_screenshot_detail`; those return OCR and metadata only, never decrypted pixels or screenshot paths. `get_personal_context` returns what the user shared about themselves, and `search_files` searches the user's chosen folders as `search-files` does, each under its own permission.

```bash
claude mcp add lokalbot -- /Applications/LokalBot.app/Contents/Helpers/lokalbot-cli mcp
```

When `lokalbot-cli` is on PATH, `claude mcp add lokalbot -- lokalbot-cli mcp` works on every platform.

`ask_library` is the synthesis tool: it sends the question to LokalBot's **local** model, which reads the library and returns only an answer with meeting citations — useful when the user wants a conclusion rather than quotes. It needs the LokalBot app running, and the first call can take up to a minute while the model loads. Prefer `search`/`get` when the user wants exact wording.

LokalBot itself does not upload library content. An external agent or MCP client may transmit tool inputs and results under its own privacy terms, so connect only clients the user trusts and retrieve the minimum meeting content needed.

## When access is off

Each kind of data needs its own permission, and one never implies another. On a Mac they are boxes under one switch: LokalBot → Settings → External Agents → "Allow external agents to read your LokalBot data", then Meetings, Screen memory, What I shared about myself, or Files. On Windows and Linux, each has its own switch under External agents in Settings → Privacy & Data: "Allow external agents to read your meeting library", "Allow external agents to read screen memory", "What I shared about myself", and "Allow external agents to search your files".

`[access_disabled]` means meetings are off, `[screen_access_disabled]` screen memory, `[personal_context_disabled]` what the user shared, and `[files_access_disabled]` Files; the message names the place. Tell the user which one it is and let them choose. Don't change consent markers or work around disabled access.

## Evidence and privacy

- Answer from returned evidence. Quote exact wording only from retrieved text; distinguish your synthesis from the recorded content. If there are no hits, say so.
- Cite meetings by title and date, adding transcript timestamps for exact moments. Identify the captured time and app for screen-memory evidence when provided.
- Never write into the meetings folder. Audio, transcripts, and summaries live in the `meetings` folder of the library root that `lokalbot-cli path` prints (on a Mac, `~/Library/Application Support/me.dotenv.LokalBot/`).
- Retrieve only the content needed. Summarize instead of pasting full transcripts unless explicitly asked.
- Do not forward transcripts, summaries, or tool results to any additional service beyond the client the user deliberately connected.
